header: Problem 5: Fullerenes. In the 80s of the 20th century, the British astrophysicist Kroto and co-workers discovered a new class of carbon allotropes whose molecular shapes are polyhedra composed of pentagons and hexagons. The most representative example is C_{60}. Its structure resembles the dome of the United States pavilion at the World Exposition in Montreal, Canada, designed by the American architect Buckminster Fuller; these molecules (not only C_{60}) are therefore called fullerenes.

subquestions.text_open: 5.1 The C_{60} molecule is a 32-faced polyhedron composed of 12 regular pentagonal faces and 20 regular hexagonal faces, and it has high symmetry. Its structure is shown below. 5.1.4 Above 30℃, C_{60} crystals can precipitate from a benzene solution. Their density is 1.65 g/cm^{3}, and the C_{60} molecules adopt cubic close packing in the crystal. Use these data to estimate the van der Waals radius of the C_{60} molecule.

subquestions.text_open:
5.3 Smaller fullerenes. In a fullerene molecule, every carbon atom is bonded to three neighboring carbon atoms. From the Lewis-structure perspective, resonance structures can therefore be drawn in which each carbon atom participates in two single bonds and one double bond. In this sense, the smallest possible fullerene could be tetrahedral C_{4} (although it has not yet been synthesized), whereas icosahedral C_{12} is not a fullerene. In this problem (5.3), you need not consider the isolated-pentagon rule. 5.3.1 Which of the following molecule(s) could be fullerenes?
(a) Octahedral C_6
(b) Cubic C_8
(c) C_{12} with the structure of the “truncated cube 3^84^6,” a polyhedron composed of regular triangles and squares whose vertices are the 12 edge midpoints of a cube
(d) Dodecahedral C_{20}

subquestions.text_open:
5.4 Alkali-Metal Compounds of Fullerenes. Several compounds of C_{60} with alkali metals have been synthesized, some of which exhibit distinctive superconducting properties. We now examine the crystal structure of a compound A of C_{60} and potassium. A belongs to the cubic crystal system. In its cubic unit cell, a C_{60} anion occupies each vertex and the body center, while each pair of opposite faces contains 4 potassium atoms. These potassium atoms form the “cage structure” composed of rhombic and hexagonal faces shown below.
5.4.2 Two potassium atoms in the crystal have fractional coordinates (1/2, 0.2795, 0) and (0.2205, 1/2, 0). Give the fractional coordinates of all remaining potassium atoms in the unit cell. Do not repeat the two coordinates already given.

text_images.description: The image shows a unit-cell diagram. Thin black lines outline a cubic unit cell, and purple spheres are located within it, with some pairs connected by purple line segments. At the lower left is a three-dimensional orthogonal coordinate system whose red, green, and blue arrows emerge from a gray central sphere: the red `a` axis points diagonally down-left, the green `b` axis points right, and the blue `c` axis points vertically upward. These axes are parallel to the three sets of unit-cell edges. There are 24 purple spheres distributed over the 6 faces of the cubic unit cell, 4 on each face. The 4 spheres on each face form a rhombus rather than a perfect square; both diagonals of the rhombus are perpendicular to the edges of the square unit-cell face, and the center of the rhombus coincides with the center of that face. Purple line segments occur in two places: along the edges of these rhombi and between the closest pair of purple spheres belonging to rhombi on adjacent unit-cell faces.
